newsitem.title: USA: Great Western reviews bid, suitor sees delay.
newsitem.headline: Great Western reviews bid, suitor sees delay.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp. said Tuesday it wanted to take all the time needed to make a careful evaluation of suitor H.F. Ahmanson and Co.'s $6.2 billion bid, but Ahmanson responded that Great Western's efforts were nothing more than delaying tactics.

Wall Street analysts and arbitragers said the rhetoric was standard for a hostile takeover battle and in the final analysis shareholders will have a chance to make their views known over the proposed takeover of tbe nation's second largest savings and loan by the No. 1 thrift.

"They're (Great Western) just insulating themselves as best as possible from Ahmanson taking a predatory position and forcing management's hand," said Todd Pitsinger, analyst at Friedman, Billings, Ramsey & Co. "They want to ensure that they have the final say."
"They have done some manoeuvring that presumably will buy some time," said a Wall Street arbitrager who did not want to be further identified.
Chatsworth, Calif.-based Great Western said it was postponing an annual shareholders meeting that had been set for April 22. A new date for the meeting was not set.
Great Western also said it has adopted a broad severance plan for employees in event of a change of control.
The company said it will oppose a solicitation of shareholder consents planned by Ahmanson.
Last Friday, Great Western amended its bylaws to stretch out the time required to obtain a shareholder vote via proxy solicitation.

After Ahmanson made a formal request last week to solicit proxies, Great Western has 10 days to announce a record date to determine which shareholders can vote. The record date must be within a maximum of 10 days of the announcement.

A spokesman for Irwindale, Calif.-based Ahmanson said the proxy solicitation would be twofold, with the first part supporting the concept of a merger and asking that steps be taken to support the Ahmanson proposal unless there is an alternative available which has better value.
The second part of the solicitation would keep Great Western from granting excessive lockup fees, breakup arrangements or stock options without the approval of shareholders.
On Tuesday, Ahmanson said Great Western was engaging in "self-serving tactics," which it said were "destructive to shareholder value and the best interests of Great Western employees."

A source close to Great Western disagreed with Ahmanson's interpretation. "The board will take its time and will carefully consider all the alternatives and will not be rushed to judgment, nor should Great Western shareholders be rushed to judgment," the source said.
Ahmanson stock dropped 75 cents to $41.50 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while Great Western rose 87.5 cents to $46.875, also on the NYSE.
